name: runbook-backup-verify
description: Prove a backup can be restored: find the newest backup and check its age and size, then - approved - restore it into a scratch location on the host, compare it (file count, checksums, or the application's own integrity check), and remove the scratch copy; then verify the result and that production was not touched.

host.description: The inventory host that holds the backups.

backups.description: Where the backups are (a directory or glob).

inspect.title: Inspect backups
inspect.prompt:
Host {{input.host}}, backups at {{input.backups}}. Read-only (ssh_exec): list them (ls -la --time-style=full-iso), the newest one's age (fail if over {{input.max_age_hours}} hours), size compared with the previous ones (a sudden drop is a red flag), and its format (tar, gzip, sql dump...). Plan the restore test: the exact commands to extract or load it into a NEW scratch directory /tmp/restore-test-<date> (never over live data), the integrity checks (tar -tzf, gzip -t, file counts, checksums against a manifest, or the application's check), and the removal of the scratch directory at the end - all in one step.

Report: the newest backup, its age and size trend, and the exact restore-test commands.

approve.title: Approve the restore test
approve.message:
Run this restore test on {{input.host}} (scratch directory only, removed afterwards)?

{{state.inspect}}

restore-test.title: Restore test
restore-test.prompt:
A person approved this restore test on {{input.host}}:
{{state.inspect}}

Run exactly those commands with ssh_exec: restore into the scratch directory, run the integrity checks, record their results, then remove the scratch directory. Nothing outside the scratch directory.

Report: each command, its result, and the integrity check outcome.

verify.title: Verify
verify.prompt:
Verify the restore test on {{input.host}}:
{{state.restore-test}}

VERIFIED when the restore completed, the integrity checks passed, the newest backup is younger than {{input.max_age_hours}} hours, and the scratch directory is gone (ssh_exec ls). Otherwise FAILED - a backup that cannot be restored is an incident: say so.

Report: the verdict and the evidence.
